page: Microsoft Azure D16als_v7 is a virtual machine instance from the Dalsv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Local storage is not bundled, though the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register average tier results. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the instance exhibits top-tier text generation speeds and strong prompt processing speeds when utilizing a small 135M parameter model, though performance scales down to average levels for larger 7B models.

Given its low-memory configuration of 2.0 GB per vCPU, the D16als_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a streamlined option for dedicated CPU processing. It is suited for workloads such as single-threaded data processing, web serving, lightweight model inference, and general-purpose compute tasks that benefit from high single-core clock speeds without high RAM requirements.

It does not include local storage but is Premium Storage capable. Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU execution, single-threaded compression, and small-model LLM text generation, while multi-core operations and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. It is well-suited for web serving, single-threaded data processing, and lightweight machine learning inference.
